evals.title: Keyword map and prompt panel for a bootstrapped SaaS, free sources only
evals.user_prompt: I run billingkit.example, invoicing software for freelancers. I have Google Search Console access but zero budget for Ahrefs or Semrush. What keywords should I target and which pages should I create? I also want to show up when people ask ChatGPT for invoicing tools.
expected_behaviors: Starts from Google Search Console queries at average positions 5-20 and labels them quick wins before proposing any new page
Validates each candidate keyword against at least two free evidence sources (autocomplete, People Also Ask, related searches, Reddit, customer words) and rejects unvalidated jargon
Maps every keyword to exactly one intent and one page using the intent table, with informational articles linking to a commercial page
Leaves search volume blank rather than inventing numbers, since no paid tool is available
Delivers the keyword map table, the placement matrix for the top 5 keywords, and a buyer prompt panel of 50-100 prompts using the four documented patterns
States that the prompt panel is the measurement input for geo-tracking and that page citability work belongs to geo-visibility
failure_modes: Recommends buying a keyword tool as a prerequisite
Invents monthly search volumes without a source
Assigns multiple distinct intents to one page, or proposes two pages for the same intent

evals.title: Two blog posts flip-flopping on the same query
evals.user_prompt: We have /blog/crm-for-small-business and /blog/best-crm-small-companies. Our ranking for 'crm for small business' keeps flip-flopping between the two URLs around position 9. Should we keep both pages?
expected_behaviors: Applies the two-search SERP test: search both keyword variants in Google and compare the top 10 result sets
Concludes that largely identical results mean same intent, therefore one page only: merge content into the stronger URL and 301 the weaker one
Explains why: two pages on one intent split internal links and ranking signals, and URL flip-flopping is the classic cannibalization symptom
Recommends consolidating inbound internal anchors to the surviving URL (seo-internal-linking) and completing the 8-point placement matrix on it
failure_modes: Recommends keeping and differentiating both pages without checking SERP overlap
Recommends deleting a page without a 301 redirect
Treats the flip-flopping as a Google bug rather than an intent collision

evals.title: Local service business targeting internal jargon
evals.user_prompt: My plumbing company in Lyon wants to rank for 'hydraulic remediation services Lyon'. Build me the keyword plan.
expected_behaviors: Flags 'hydraulic remediation services' as internal jargon and validates what buyers actually type (emergency plumber Lyon, water leak repair Lyon) via autocomplete, People Also Ask, and forum phrasing
Applies the local pattern: keyword plus city in title, URL, H1, meta description, first paragraph, and image alt, with a pointer to seo-local for the full local workflow
Prioritizes long-tail emergency and job-specific queries that convert quickly, while planning head terms over time
Adds local buyer prompts (best plumber in Lyon, is [brand] plumbing reliable) to a prompt panel handed to geo-tracking
failure_modes: Builds the plan around the jargon keyword as requested, without language validation
Omits the keyword plus city placement pattern
Targets only the broad head term 'plumber Lyon' with no long tail
